prior_announcement.credit: Nicolà Schnieper, Orbit closures and G-irreducibility, University of Bern master’s thesis, 2024
prior_announcement.announcement_source: Kummer–Riener, Journal of Algebra 666 (2025), printed page 42; bibliography printed page 46, reference [21]
prior_announcement.description_of_this_work: Complete alternative proof of a previously announced result

accepted_claims: For every finite positive n and algebraically closed field K, Q=KQ(Spec(K[x_ij])/G) is spectral, with ordinary prime points and finite-support row permutations G.
Every proper G-stable radical G-prime ideal is the intersection of the translates of an ordinary prime ideal.
The topological orbit quotient followed by its Kolmogorov quotient is sober; equivariant Noetherianity supplies all remaining spectral axioms.
Every G-stable closed subset of the ordinary spectrum is a finite union of orbit closures.
interpretation_caveats: The original primary-source setting assumes K is uncountable; the proof works for any algebraically closed K.
All prime ideals are points, including nonclosed points; replacing Spec by K-rational points changes the problem.
The group is the union of finite symmetric groups, not a substituted full-permutation orbit space.
The quotient is topological orbit quotient then Kolmogorov quotient, not Spec of the invariant ring or a GIT quotient.
The countable-ring lemma needs reducedness; the scalar-extension domain lemma needs algebraic closedness.
Infinite intersections commute with field scalar extension of vector spaces; no assertion about arbitrary flat ring extensions is used.
Hillar–Sullivant Theorem 1.1 / Corollary 3.5 is a specialized import; relevant statements and finite-support applicability were checked, but the foundational Gröbner/Higman proof was not reaudited.
Cohen’s original paper and Schnieper’s thesis were not retrieved; the former is historical attribution and the latter is credited prior announcement.
No formal proof-assistant certification, external human peer review, exhaustive literature search, first-resolution claim, or novelty certificate is supplied.
review_status: AI-assisted, unrefereed, internal AI mathematical audit
